comparator.name: European Languages and Cultures
comparator.route: German major language — European Language and Society profile
comparator.sourceNotes: This 180 EC example follows the German major language and European Language and Society profile in the 2026–2027 regulations. It includes all three first German-specific modules, the later interdisciplinary German module, 10 EC of restricted electives, a 30 EC minor and a 10 EC thesis.
components: Starts the German Plus language sequence.
Introduction to European Language and Society
Introduction to Culture and Literature: Text and Context
Introduction to European Politics and Society
Stories We Live By: Mediating Identities Through Language, Media, Culture and Literature
One of two faculty-wide choices in the first year.
Follows German Plus 2 and develops academic communication in German.
Choose profile enrichment, a second profile or a second language.
Applies linguistics to Standard German after German Plus 2.
Stories We Live By: Narrating the World
One of four faculty-wide choices in the second year.
Studies German literature after German Plus 2.
Studies German politics and political culture after German Plus 2.
A minor at Groningen or approved study abroad. Study abroad has credit and course prerequisites.
Language Specific module German 2: Interdisciplinary study of Language, Literature & Politics
Requires German Plus 3 and two of the three first German-specific modules.
Bachelor's Thesis European Languages and Cultures
Requires all first-year credits and specified later profile and language modules. A major-language thesis is also available.

routeSelection.route: German major language — European Language and Society profile
routeSelection.basis: The public programme lists German first among eight major languages and Language and Society first among three profiles. The regulations and dated catalogue support both choices. The order resolves the representative-route tie without reference to UCR course availability.

courses: New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory

alternatives.label: Language, culture & society in Europe
alternatives.concept: Study how language works and how it shapes public life. Begin with everyday Dutch, rhetoric and the study of language and thought. Apply those perspectives to literary texts, media and social debates, with modern European history and EU politics as regional anchors.
alternatives.labelReason: Dutch, stylistics, psycholinguistics and rhetoric lead the route. Modern History and European Union Politics provide European context alongside wider cultural and social comparisons.
progression: Foundations in brain and behaviour precede Psycholinguistics. Rhetorical analysis precedes advanced persuasion and community work. History, sociology and media studies support later analysis of public culture. The plan includes 9 courses at the 300 level.

alternatives.label: Literature, media & cultural identity
alternatives.concept: Follow stories and images across literature, film and visual art. Move from close reading and Renaissance art to adaptation, documentary and the history of art interpretation. Use these methods to examine how identity and power are represented across societies.
alternatives.labelReason: The route progresses from literary and visual interpretation to research on narratives, film and art. The Italian Renaissance and European documentary traditions add regional examples within a wider cultural comparison.
alternatives.distinctness: The literature and media and the language and society options differ by 52.5 EC each way. Literary history and criticism, myth, visual art and adaptation take the place of Dutch, psycholinguistics, EU politics and several social science courses.
progression: Introductory literary criticism and stylistics support later theory, adaptation and documentary. Renaissance visual culture and introductory film analysis lead into advanced work on how images and texts are interpreted. The plan includes 8 courses at the 300 level.

alternatives.label: Modern Europe, politics & social change
alternatives.concept: Study modern Europe through history, political institutions and conflict. Build from political philosophy and comparative politics to EU decision-making, international relations and research on social change. Use media and literature to explore how public debates take shape.
alternatives.labelReason: Modern history, European Union Politics and comparative politics anchor the route. Historical and qualitative inquiry, peace studies and social theory support the study of political and social change.
alternatives.distinctness: The politics option differs by 75 EC from the language option and 75 EC from the literature option in each direction. Its distinctive core is political philosophy, comparative politics, international relations, historical research and conflict.
progression: Foundations in history, politics and sociology lead to international relations, EU institutions and advanced historical research. Social theory, civic communication and environmental justice extend the analysis of political change. The plan includes 10 courses at the 300 level.

candidates.label: Cumulative European-language proficiency
candidates.assessment: The workbook supports beginner Dutch for everyday use. It has no cumulative proficiency sequence in any of the eight languages and no German-medium sequence in linguistics, literature and politics. Analysing texts, speech or bilingual learning cannot supply that progression.

selection.assessment: Three coherent schedules cover the main interests through language and society, literature and cultural identity, and politics and social change. Each pair differs by at least 30 EC in each direction. The separate proficiency direction has insufficient language instruction across all eight languages.

notes.text: Groningen combines a three-course German proficiency sequence with academic study in German. The UCR options offer introductory Dutch, linguistics, literature, media or European politics in different combinations.
The UCR course options do not include a German proficiency sequence or the specialist modules taught in German. Groningen’s minor and required thesis are shown separately in the curriculum.

blocks: Both examine linguistic structure, including word and sentence patterns. UCR applies this to meaning in texts, while Groningen compares the structures of European languages.
Both study how the mind processes language. Groningen focuses on psycho- and neurolinguistic research methods.
Both analyse how stories shape identity. UCR focuses on memoir, autobiography and travel writing.
Both interpret and produce narratives. UCR works in the specific form of nonfiction film.
Both introduce the interpretation of literature. Groningen places texts in a European cultural context.
Both examine modern European history. Groningen also introduces linguistic and political ways to study Europe.
Both examine democracy and political institutions. UCR uses a wider comparative scope.
Academic skills, Groningen requirements & independent work

Groningen applies linguistic analysis to Standard German.
Groningen examines first- and second-language learning through theory and research.
Groningen analyses literary genres and periods in German.
Groningen studies German political culture and its European context in the major language.
Groningen reserves 30 EC for a minor or approved study abroad.
This advanced German module brings together linguistics, literature and politics.
Groningen teaches linguistic research design, corpus or questionnaire work and basic statistical analysis.
Groningen requires a 10 EC thesis. The optional UCR research shown alongside it is separate from the course schedules.

audience.programmeDescription: Groningen’s degree combines study of a major European language with questions about language, literature and politics. The example shown follows German and the European Language and Society profile.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The UCR options focus on language and society, literature and media, or modern European politics. The Groningen example includes advanced language study in German.
